Closing a worktree can strand a running terminal at a deleted cwd

Bugs·seedling·proposed·JUL 04, 2026

A failed PTY kill is swallowed at every layer — the padi endpoint unregisters anyway and the client evicts anyway — so the worktree is removed out from under a still-running shell. Fix (one PR) — surface the kill failure as a typed error, keep the entry, and abort the worktree removal, mirroring the sleeping-terminal discard path that already does this.

Plan of record · branch aged-break · issue #1666 · status: proposed

The Close and remove worktree action closes a terminal and then deletes its git worktree. If the close’s PTY kill fails, the flow deletes the worktree anyway — leaving a still-running shell sitting in a directory that no longer exists. The issue was filed from the W4 comprehensiveness sweep as a code-path defect: a swallowed error nobody had turned into a real failure yet.

Root cause — the failure signal is dropped twice

A kill failure has to travel back up from kaval to the client for the worktree removal to know to stop. It never arrives. The padi endpoint catches the pty-host kill error and unregisters the terminal anyway, then returns success (terminalEndpoint/local.ts:956 — “pty-host kill failed; unregistering anyway”). The client’s handleKill then swallows any error and evicts the tile anyway (useTerminalCrud.ts:242 — catch {}). So handleKillWorktree sees a clean success and removes the worktree. The one error code the client can see today — NOT_FOUND — is the benign “already exited” case, so the issue’s one-line “just check the client” framing would fix nothing: there is no genuine failure to catch until the endpoint stops hiding it.

What a user sees

Today, closing a worktree whose terminal can’t be killed silently removes the worktree and drops the tile — the shell keeps running, orphaned, in a deleted directory, with no UI handle left to stop it. After this fix, the worktree is kept, the tile stays, and a toast explains why — so the user can retry once the terminal host is reachable again. This is exactly how closing a sleeping terminal’s worktree already behaves when its discard fails; the fix brings the active path in line.

today — broken
  1. you pick “Close and remove worktree”
  2. the terminal host is unreachable → the PTY kill fails
  3. endpoint unregisters anyway · client evicts anyway
✗ worktree deleted · tile gone · a live shell stranded at a path that no longer exists
this plan — fixed
  1. you pick “Close and remove worktree”
  2. the PTY kill fails → the endpoint surfaces it, keeps the terminal
  3. handleKill returns false → the removal is aborted
⚠Failed to close terminal: the terminal host is unreachable, so the kill could not be confirmed
✓ worktree kept · tile stays · retry when the host is back

There is no new UI, no new setting, no new affordance — the only visible change is that a failed close now shows an error toast (the repo’s standard toast.error, red via richColors) and doesn’t destroy anything. On the happy path (the kill succeeds, the overwhelmingly common case) nothing changes at all.

Architecture — one chokepoint, one contract inversion

The fix is one coherent change threading three existing seams — it warrants a single PR, not a staged rollout.

The volatility this touches is already bounded — this is a leaf change, not a new boundary. Nothing here is a domain-agnostic capability hiding a hard volatility, so no new @kolu/* package is involved. It edits the terminal lifecycle in place: one server chokepoint (endpoint.killTerminal), one typed error beside an existing one, and two client handlers.

Reuse the source of truth — the abort pattern already exists. The sleeping-terminal path solved this exact problem for the discard case: handleDiscard returns false on a surfaced failure, and handleKillWorktree bails before removing the worktree (useWorktreeOps.ts:86 — if (!discarded) return;). The active path just never got the mirror guard. So handleKill learns to return a boolean the same way handleDiscard does, and the active branch gains the same if (!allKilled) return;. No parallel mechanism is invented; the fix makes two siblings symmetric.

Fail fast — the swallow is the defect. The endpoint’s “catch → unregister anyway → return success” is textbook graceful-degradation: it pretends a kill succeeded so the UI stays tidy, at the cost of a destructive follow-up firing on an unconfirmed result. The interface contract even documents this as intentional (endpoint.ts:131 — “it still unregisters (so a failed kill never strands a dead entry in the UI) and relies on reattach-time reconciliation … to reap any surviving orphan”). This fix inverts that contract: on a genuine failure the endpoint keeps the entry and throws, so the caller can decline a destructive follow-up and the user can retry. That doc comment is rewritten as part of the change.

Why keeping the entry is safe (not a stuck tile)

A genuine pty-host kill failure means the kaval transport failed — and a local unix socket doesn’t blip while the process lives, so in practice kaval itself is down and its PTYs died with it. Keeping the entry can’t strand a live shell against a healthy kaval, because a healthy kaval never fails the kill. The kept entry is not a permanent zombie: (a) a retry-kill closes it once kaval is reachable (kaval’s kill is idempotent — ptyHost.ts:859); (b) the boot adopt-or-reap reconcile drops a saved active entry whose PTY is gone and re-adopts one still alive (reconcile.ts — unit-pinned in reconcile.test.ts); and (c) “Restart kaval” drains and re-parks everything. This mirrors releaseSleptPty, which already keeps its (sleeping) record on a kill failure and leans on the same reconcile.One honest residual: killTerminal tears sensors down before the kill (local.ts:955, deliberately — so the kill’s own exit event can’t double-fire handleExit). A kept entry is therefore sensorless until a retry/recycle/boot re-arms it. But this window is exactly when the whole kaval endpoint is degraded and every tile is stale anyway, so the fix simply keeps this one tile present (so it’s retryable) instead of vanishing it. Re-arming sensors on the failure path is both impossible — the link is down, you can’t subscribe — and redundant, since every recovery path rebuilds from the saved session. So the fix does not attempt it.

Implementation

Three edits plus tests and docs. File-level integration points, in dependency order:

1 · Mint the typed error — packages/padi/src/terminal-registry.ts, beside terminalNotFound (line 291). oRPC scrubs bare errors to an opaque “Internal server error”, so the failure must be a typed ORPCError to reach the client with a legible message. A custom code round-trips fine (the repo already ships one — SURFACE_STDIO_FRAME_DECODE_FAILED in surface/src/links/stdio-codec.ts):

export function terminalKillFailed(id: string): ORPCError<"TERMINAL_KILL_FAILED", undefined> {
  return new ORPCError("TERMINAL_KILL_FAILED", {
    message: `Terminal ${id}: the terminal host is unreachable, so the kill could not be confirmed`,
  });
}

2 · Stop swallowing at the endpoint — packages/padi/src/terminalEndpoint/local.ts:956-960. Replace the catch-and-unregister with a throw that keeps the entry (do not call cleanupTerminalScratch / finalizeRemoval on this path):

try {
  await ptyHostClient.surface.terminal.kill({ id });
} catch (err) {
  tlog.error({ err }, "pty-host kill failed; keeping the entry so the PTY isn't orphaned");
  throw terminalKillFailed(id);
}
cleanupTerminalScratch(id);
this.finalizeRemoval(id);
return entry.info;

The !info → terminalNotFound translation in the surface handler (servePadi.ts:290) is unchanged: killTerminal still returns undefined for a not-active id (the benign NOT_FOUND), and now throws the distinct TERMINAL_KILL_FAILED for a genuine failure. Rewrite the TerminalEndpoint interface doc (endpoint.ts:128-134) to describe the new contract (keep-and-throw on a genuine failure; undefined still means “was not an active terminal”).

3 · Distinguish and abort in the client — packages/client/src/terminal/. Add import { ORPCError } from "@orpc/client"; to useTerminalCrud.ts (the repo’s sole idiom for reading a code — useTerminals.ts:80). Make handleKill return a boolean, evicting on success or the benign NOT_FOUND, and surfacing-without-evicting on a genuine failure (mirrors handleDiscard, useTerminalCrud.ts:320):

async function handleKill(id: TerminalId): Promise<boolean> {
  try {
    await padiRpc(padi).surface.lifecycle.kill({ id });
  } catch (err) {
    // NOT_FOUND = already exited → benign; fall through and evict.
    if (!(err instanceof ORPCError && err.code === "NOT_FOUND")) {
      toast.error(`Failed to close terminal: ${(err as Error).message}`);
      return false; // the PTY may still be alive — do NOT evict
    }
  }
  removeAndAutoSwitch(id);
  return true;
}

Then gate the worktree removal in useWorktreeOps.ts:88-92 (the active else-branch), mirroring the sleeping arm’s if (!discarded) return;:

} else {
  const subs = store.getSubTerminalIds(id);
  let allKilled = true;
  for (const subId of subs) allKilled = (await deps.handleKill(subId)) && allKilled;
  allKilled = (await deps.handleKill(id)) && allKilled;
  if (!allKilled) return; // don't strand a live shell at a deleted cwd
}

handleKill’s other callers (App.tsx, handleKillWithSubs, handleSleep’s sub-kills) ignore the return via void/await — unaffected, and they inherit the honest new behavior (a failed close now surfaces instead of silently evicting).

Tests — two red repros, one per swallow point

Both run under vitest’s default node env (no DOM); neither package sets an environment. Run one file with pnpm --filter @kolu/padi exec vitest run <file> / pnpm --filter kolu-client exec vitest run <file> (wrapped in the nix shell, as just test-unit does).

  • Server — new packages/padi/src/terminalEndpoint/killTerminal.test.ts. Template: ptyHost/restartLocal.test.ts (its fakeEndpoint + __setEndpointForTest, ptyHost/index.ts:183) plus sleepWake.test.ts’s registry seeding (registerTerminal + setPadiSurfaceCtx + setDaemonProcessId). The kill’s real seam is the module-level ptyHostClient, not the endpoint arg of buildPadiSurfaceDeps (that backs only fs/git). Red fact: with an active terminal and a fake whose surface.terminal.kill rejects, killTerminal(id) currently resolves and unregisters — the test asserts it rejects with a code ≠ NOT_FOUND and getTerminal(id) is still defined. Control: an absent id → returns undefined (→ NOT_FOUND).
  • Client — new packages/client/src/terminal/useWorktreeOps.test.ts. Template: useSessionRestore.test.ts (mock ../wire → { padi: {} }, @kolu/padi/surface → both padiRpc and sleepingArm, and solid-sonner; hoisted spies; a stub store). Deps are injected, so pass a stub handleKill. Red fact: with an active-worktree meta and handleKill resolving false, handleKillWorktree(id) currently still calls worktreeRemove — the test asserts it is never called. Controls: handleKill → true removes it; the sleeping arm (handleDiscard → false) still aborts (regression guard).

  • website/src/content/changelog/unreleased.mdx — one line under ### Fixed (a user-facing correctness fix). PR link backfilled after the PR exists.
  • Grep of README.md / packages/*/README.md / website/ / docs/atlas/ for the touched terms surfaced no user-facing prose describing the old swallow behavior (only changelog #1633, an unrelated already-shipped fix), so no marketing/README edits are needed — this note is the doc home.

Evidence angle

This is a fault-injection fix — the failure only fires when the terminal host is unreachable, which no e2e scenario reaches organically. The primary proof is the two red→green repros; the visible artifact is the error toast plus the surviving worktree directory. Evidence is captured at ship time per the run’s PR-evidence procedure.
